stories.title: Vogue India highlights homegrown labels
stories.summary: Vogue India's 2026 Best Dressed list is pivoting from international logos toward homegrown labels. The publication notes that the Indian fashion landscape is shifting from a focus on brand names to intention and point of view. Turning inward is now a guaranteed way to make a statement.

stories.title: The fear of being perceived in fashion
stories.summary: Personal style often hits a wall when the desire to look cool meets the fear of being seen trying. Trying new accessories or patterns can feel like a public performance, as the gap between one's moodboard and one's actual wardrobe remains defined by the dread of being perceived.

stories.title: Sonam Kapoor and Diljit Dosanjh share style tips
stories.summary: Vogue India's 2026 stars offer advice on elevating looks. Sonam Kapoor suggests treating every garment as an heirloom, while Diljit Dosanjh advocates for merging Indian jewellery with contemporary silhouettes. The goal is to break stylistic conventions by intentionally clashing patterns or wearing contrasting colours.

stories.title: Vogue India shares 11 style lessons
stories.summary: Vogue India has released 11 styling lessons from its 2026 best-dressed list. The publication advises that personal style is less about trends and more about knowing when to break rules. Recommendations include embracing ornate anarkalis and treating even brand new clothing as a timeless heirloom.

stories.title: Models discuss the reality of the industry
stories.summary: Bhavitha Mandava and Diya Joukani recently discussed their paths into the fashion industry. Mandava, a product design student scouted while waiting for a bus, and Joukani, who studied international relations, noted that their professional lives did not go to plan. They are now paid to walk.

stories.title: A guide to alternative Indian fashion
stories.summary: A new guide explores the roots of subcultures like punk, goth, and emo within India. It examines how Alt TikTok has transformed countercultural rebellion into an aesthetic. The resource aims to help readers discover labels that push back against mainstream consumerism and fast fashion trends.

stories.title: Textiles minister reviews Tamil Nadu initiatives
stories.summary: Union Minister of Textiles Giriraj Singh reviewed textile sector initiatives in Tamil Nadu on 23 and 24 November 2026. The meetings focused on weaver welfare, product diversification, and export promotion. Officials from the Central Silk Board and PM MITRA Park participated in the review of industry verticals.

stories.title: Mauve brings handlooms to luxury fashion
stories.summary: Luxury fashion house Mauve is positioning handloom sarees and artisanal jewellery as contemporary luxury. Founded by Neetu and Vaenya Singhal, the brand operates on the belief that traditions remain timeless when each generation finds a new way to make them its own.

stories.title: Black Friday gains traction in Indian retail
stories.summary: Black Friday is emerging as a significant retail event in India between Diwali and Christmas. Retailers are using the four-day window to clear unsold festive inventory and prepare shelf space for winter collections. Fashion retailers are shifting focus from ethnic wear to western and winter clothing.

stories.title: Malin Åkerman reflects on 27 Dresses
stories.summary: Malin Åkerman revisited her role as Tess in the 2008 film 27 Dresses. While some view the character as a villain for stealing her sister's crush, Åkerman describes her as a young, stupid girl who learned a life lesson. It is less villain, more just human.

stories.title: Packing for Vegas as a Vogue editor
stories.summary: Packing for the Las Vegas F1 Grand Prix has challenged a Vogue editor accustomed to minimalist fashion capitals. The glitz of Sin City falls outside the usual reliable formula developed during countless fashion months. The destination has successfully thrown the standard packing blueprint for a loop.

stories.title: Fashion Trust U.S. hosts Sergio Hudson dinner
stories.summary: Sergio Hudson was celebrated at a Fashion Trust U.S. dinner in West Hollywood on 20 November. The event brought together various Hollywood figures, including Brandy and Sheryl Lee Ralph. The evening was described as swanky and lush, with a strictly invite-only atmosphere.

stories.title: Children of the revolution: how the north of England is defining modern men’s fashion - The Guardian
Jonathan Anderson presents Dior Cruise 2027
stories.summary: Jonathan Anderson's Dior Cruise 2027 show at LACMA utilised modern technology to reconstruct the aesthetic of 1940s and 1950s Los Angeles. Anderson described the process as reverse engineering, aiming to build a bridge toward the past using present-day tools to create surreal and playful volumes.

stories.title: Zahia Dehar outfit sparks online debate
stories.summary: Zahia Dehar wore a black bandeau and skirt to the GQ Men of the Year 2026 event in Paris, prompting online discourse regarding the design. Some social media users questioned the construction of the look, with one commenter suggesting the tape was fighting for its life.

stories.title: Simone Ashley wears Gucci archival piece
stories.summary: Simone Ashley attended the Only Murders in the Building season six premiere in a blue ombre mini dress. The garment, originally designed by Tom Ford for Gucci's 2003 collection, was previously worn by Kim Kardashian. Ashley paired the archival piece with open-toed heels for the London event.

stories.title: Simone Ashley and Kim Kardashian share Gucci look
stories.summary: Simone Ashley wore a 2003 Gucci dress to the London premiere of Only Murders in the Building on 23 November. The blue mini dress, featuring floral details and a high neckline, was previously worn by Kim Kardashian. Both stars styled the vintage designer piece differently.

stories.title: Jewellers in Bengaluru face stock value concerns
stories.summary: Falling gold and silver prices have renewed interest in jewellery stores ahead of the December wedding season. While the correction is encouraging customers to return, jewellers are now concerned about the value of existing inventory purchased at higher rates. The market remains volatile.

stories.title: India gold and silver market remains volatile
stories.summary: Bullion prices saw a recovery earlier this week, drawing buyers back into the market. However, uncertainty regarding global interest rates, the US dollar, and inflation data continues to drive volatility. Retail figures from November 24 are the latest available for tracking the ongoing price fluctuations.

stories.title: Prada expands Couleur Vivante fine jewelry collection
stories.summary: Prada has added new 2026 designs to its Couleur Vivante fine jewelry collection, including a mini necklace and stud earrings. The pieces feature the brand's triangular Prada Cut and white gold settings. The collection will be available in select stores following a made-to-order phase.

stories.title: Cartier debuts Le Choeur des Pierres collection
stories.summary: Cartier has unveiled its latest high jewelry collection, featuring a selection of fancy-colored diamonds. The brand says the collection name reflects a chorus of gems, with the creative process starting from the character of each individual stone rather than a pre-determined design.

stories.title: Jane Win adds bridal focus to coin jewelry
stories.summary: Jane Win is expanding its signature coin jewelry into the bridal market. The brand says brides are selecting coins with words like LOVE or LUCKY for bridesmaids. The company reports that customers have viewed the jewelry as a personal way to make gifts special since its inception.

stories.title: Guilford and Company highlights antique jewelry designs
stories.summary: Guilford and Company is showcasing its collection of antique jewelry. The firm emphasizes timeless and classic designs as part of its current inventory. The business continues to operate with a focus on traditional styles for its customers.

stories.title: Tanishq business model targets trust in retail
stories.summary: Tanishq, owned by Titan, was built to turn India's relationship-driven jewellery trade into a branded retail business. The company says it aimed to fill a gap in the market by providing a trusted, scalable alternative to traditional family jewellers. It remains a central name in the industry.

8ct. Pink-Diamond Ring Scores Nearly $15M at Christie’s - Rapaport
DJI releases pearl white Osmo Pocket 4P
stories.summary: DJI has introduced a pearl white version of its Osmo Pocket 4P camera. The company suggests the device is designed to integrate into daily life and street style, moving away from the traditional matte black finish typically associated with professional imaging equipment.

stories.title: Fossil launches Avengers Doomsday watch collection
stories.summary: Fossil is releasing four limited-edition watches inspired by the upcoming Marvel Studios film Avengers: Doomsday. The collection features designs based on Doctor Doom, Thor, Gambit, and Mister Fantastic. The watches will be available on November 26, ahead of the film's December 18 theatrical release.

stories.title: Georg Jensen promotes holiday gifts as heirlooms
stories.summary: Danish design house Georg Jensen is marketing its holiday collection as enduring objects intended to be passed between generations. Creative director Paula Gerbase says the brand aims to create items that hold resonance beyond their physical form, distinguishing them from ephemeral gifts like food or experiences.

stories.title: Expert outlines basics of classic men's watches
stories.summary: A guide to classic men's watches aims to demystify the category for those who find the market intimidating. The expert suggests that many timepieces are either over-hyped or overlooked, and provides a breakdown of entry-level information for those seeking to understand these status symbols.

stories.title: Bucket bags maintain popularity in 2026
stories.summary: The bucket bag remains a staple in 2026, balancing a slouchy hobo aesthetic with a structured tote. Originally designed in the 1930s to transport Champagne, the silhouette is now a canvas for designers to experiment with proportions and materials. It continues to be marketed for its versatility.

stories.title: Stylish boots marketed for festive season
stories.summary: Retailers are promoting eight boot styles for the festive season, targeting both winter getaways and everyday wear. Despite Singapore's climate, the campaign suggests that shoppers can still participate in the trend through various silhouettes, including star-studded heels and tall boots.

stories.title: European Commission probes composite material imports
stories.summary: The European Commission has launched a safeguard investigation into glass-fibre reinforcements and chemical inputs from all countries. Citing global overcapacity and rising import pressures, the commission says these materials are strategic for wind energy and defence. Provisional measures may follow within five months.

stories.title: Ronnie Fieg and ASICS release Darth Vader shoes
stories.summary: Ronnie Fieg and ASICS have collaborated on a Darth Vader-inspired version of the 2008 GEL-LYTE III. The shoe features perforated nubuck, leather overlays, and character insoles. Retailing for $220, the collection releases globally via Kith on November 25.

stories.title: Vibram FiveFingers gains fashion industry attention
stories.summary: Vibram is positioning its FiveFingers toe shoes as a fashion item. Global SVP Carmen Marani says the brand previously faced barriers due to the shoe's aesthetic, which was historically associated with marathoners. The company is now focused on its adoption by women in the fashion industry.

stories.title: Dastkar Bazaar 2026 to open in Hyderabad
stories.summary: The Dastkar Bazaar 2026 will run from November 27 to December 3 at Kamma Sangham Hall. Organised by Hands on Dastkar, the exhibition promises a confluence of artisans and craftspeople from across India. Hyderabad residents are invited to explore regional textiles and home decor without leaving the city.

stories.title: Ferraro to showcase finishing solutions at India ITME 2026
stories.summary: Italy's Ferraro SpA will present its tubular and open-width fabric finishing machinery at India ITME 2026. Established in 1951, the company highlights its seven decades of experience and specialized solutions like COMPTEX REvolution. It aims to assist manufacturers seeking consistent fabric quality and reliable finishing results.

stories.title: Savio to present smart spinning and winding tech
stories.summary: Savio will display its Proxima Smartconer, Lybra Smartspinner, and other winding and twisting solutions at India ITME 2026. The company claims these technologies target higher efficiency, flexibility, and yarn quality for Indian mills. The equipment includes remote monitoring capabilities through the company's proprietary Insight platform.

stories.title: Mario Crosta marks centenary at India ITME
stories.summary: Mario Crosta will highlight its textile finishing technology at India ITME, following its 2025 centenary. The company reports installations in 75 countries with a global base exceeding 10,000 units. It continues to focus on precision engineering and specialized fabric surface treatments for manufacturers seeking improved product quality.

stories.title: Textile industry faces 20 percent growth requirement
stories.summary: The Indian textile and apparel industry must achieve over 20 percent annual growth to reach a 100 billion dollar export target by FY31, according to Boston Consulting Group. The sector is currently valued at 190 to 200 billion dollars and requires modernized manufacturing to gain global market share.

stories.title: Denim import shifts highlight European market contest
stories.summary: Bangladesh remains the European Union's top denim supplier, though imports fell in the first nine months of 2026. Egypt gained market share nearly equal to the decline seen in Bangladesh, while China saw a recovery. Data suggests a 2027 contest over finishing speeds for European jeans orders.

stories.title: EU imposes anti-dumping duties on Chinese PET spunbond
stories.summary: The European Union has implemented five-year duties on Chinese PET spunbond nonwovens to protect a 200 million euro technical-textile market. Despite the measures, import data shows Chinese volume continues to rise. Customs classification gaps suggest that duties alone may not be sufficient to restore regional industrial strength.

stories.title: New research addresses fashion resale supply
stories.summary: A report from the Ellen MacArthur Foundation suggests fashion businesses are struggling to scale resale due to a lack of predictable supply. The research identifies customer wardrobes as an untapped source of high-quality items, noting that current trade-in programs are failing to capture the majority of discarded clothing.

stories.title: Naphtha and PX prices decline
Press Release: New research shows how fashion businesses can unlock second-hand supply
stories.summary: Billions of existing clothes, accessories, and shoes are unworn or thrown away too soon, never to be given a second life. Resale and remaking can help address this, but a lack of predictable, high-quality supply is preventing businesses from meeting growing demand. Fashion businesses struggling to scale resale and remaking

stories.title: Survey finds most shoppers clear out wardrobes annually
stories.summary: An Ellen MacArthur Foundation report based on an Accenture UK survey found that nine in 10 people cleared out their wardrobes in the past year. Most shoppers described the discarded items as being in good condition, yet few utilized brand trade-in programs to keep the clothing in circulation.

stories.title: Retail can turn customers into 'suppliers' as closet clearouts power resale growth - report - FashionNetwork - The World
Report highlights fashion reuse supply gaps
stories.summary: The Ellen MacArthur Foundation reports that fashion brands risk losing reusable clothing to household waste. The research finds that abundant unwanted garments are not reaching resale channels because collection processes remain difficult. Brands are urged to coordinate more effectively with existing secondhand operators to capture this supply.

stories.title: STICA week to address fashion decarbonisation
stories.summary: The European Textile Initiative for Climate Action will host a week of events from November 30 to December 4. The program will examine climate finance, factory emissions, and worker protection. Participants include manufacturers, researchers, and campaigners tasked with discussing who pays for the industry's required emissions cuts.

stories.title: Sustainability gains focus in fine jewelry
stories.summary: A 2025 Blue Yonder survey of 5,000 consumers suggests that shoppers are increasingly applying the same scrutiny to jewelry sourcing as they do to food and clothing. While tradition has historically prioritized the sentiment of jewelry, sustainability is becoming a more significant factor in consumer purchasing decisions.

Authentic Brands Group partners with Genesys for retail operations
stories.summary: Authentic Brands Group is partnering with AI platform Genesys to manage sales across marketplaces. The company oversees 1,700 licensees and 50 brands including Reebok and Champion. Traditionally, partners had to integrate systems with each marketplace individually. Now, they can integrate once to reach 400 platforms.

stories.title: AI demand forecasts fail to lower holiday discounts
stories.summary: Brands are increasingly using AI to forecast demand and narrow the depth of their holiday discounts. Despite these efforts, Salesforce data shows November discount rates are up 5 percent globally and 8 percent in the U.S. year over year. The machines are learning, but the sales are rising.

stories.title: Meta launches AI shopping agent Muse in the UK
stories.summary: Meta has launched its AI shopping agent Muse in the UK, allowing customers to search and buy products without browsing individual websites. Retailers including Sainsbury’s, M&S, and Asos have signed on to the technology. The development brings agentic commerce into the mainstream, provided the agents can find the items.

stories.title: Meta Launches AI Agent Muse in UK - The Business of Fashion
SSENSE pulls virtual try-on images after designer complaints
stories.summary: Luxury retailer SSENSE has removed product images from its website after designers accused the company of misrepresenting their clothes. The retailer acknowledged using virtual try-on technology to generate the imagery. Designers highlighted discrepancies between their actual garments and the digital versions. The technology has been asked to step back.

stories.title: Matters.AI raises $12 million in pre-Series A funding
stories.summary: Matters.AI has raised $12 million in a pre-Series A round led by Tanglin Venture Partners. The platform uses agents that combine data understanding with behavior context to investigate risks autonomously. The company says it keeps human approval as the boundary before its agents rotate credentials.

stories.title: Wonderscent launches AI fragrance discovery platform
stories.summary: Wonderscent has launched an AI platform that recommends fragrances based on mood or vibe descriptions. The company says buying perfume online is currently a one-size-fits-all experience. Users can now search a catalog of 50,000 fragrances by describing a feeling, such as a forest after rain.

stories.title: Limited Edt opens fourth store in New Delhi
stories.summary: Limited Edt has opened its fourth store in India at Avenue Mall, Saket. The company says the new space represents countless hours of planning and dedication. The retailer aims to bring global sneaker and streetwear culture closer to its community through the expansion.

stories.title: Reebok opens second store in Tripura
stories.summary: Reebok has opened its second store in the capital city of Tripura, India. The brand says the move is a step toward strengthening its presence and bringing its world of sport and style closer to consumers in the Northeast. The company entered the Indian market in 1995.

stories.title: Indian manufacturers to meet European fashion buyers in Copenhagen
stories.summary: The Apparel Export Promotion Council is bringing Indian garment manufacturers to Copenhagen on January 28 and 29, 2027. The event aims to connect local suppliers with European brands and retailers. The council is pitching the meet to buyers largely on cost and duty savings. Meetings are scheduled.
